content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Joins and concatenation connect datasets; validate key relationships so duplicated keys do not multiply rows unexpectedly.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Join validation expresses a business rule about key cardinality. Use `validate="one_to_one"`, `"one_to_many"`, or `"many_to_one"` when that relationship is expected; inspect duplicate keys rather than assuming the merge is safe.

content_blocks.code:
import pandas as pd

orders = pd.DataFrame({"customer_id": [1, 2]})
customers = pd.DataFrame({"customer_id": [1, 2], "name": ["Ari", "Bo"]})
print(len(orders.merge(customers, on="customer_id", validate="one_to_one")))
